How the attribution works

Trace. From the suspect wallet, Ronn Tech follows outgoing transfers hop by hop, keeping the three largest recipients at each step and any recipient of at least 10% of the outflow. Transfers under $10 are ignored. Only native coins, USDT and USDC count, matched by contract address so fake look-alike tokens are never followed.

Recognise exchanges. Every wallet reached is checked against real labels built into this page: exchange proof-of-reserve wallets (DefiLlama, tier A), Etherscan-derived labels (tier B) and the OFAC sanctions list.

Find deposit addresses. An unlabelled wallet that forwards at least 99% of what it received to an exchange wallet within 11 hours is treated as that exchange's deposit address (Victor, Financial Cryptography 2020). On Bitcoin, a wallet spent together with an exchange wallet in one transaction joins that exchange's cluster.

Score. Each path scores R × H × √V × T: label reliability, hop decay (1, 1, 0.85, 0.70), the share of the suspect's outflow that arrived, and timing (1.0 within 72 hours per hop, 0.8 within 30 days, otherwise 0.6). Paths to the same exchange combine as 1 − Π(1 − score). High is 75 and above, Medium 50–74, Low 25–49.

Limits. Labels can be incomplete; inference is a heuristic; free APIs return recent history only; USD values use today's price. Attribution is an investigative lead, not proof of ownership. Only the exchange's KYC records establish who controls an account.
